Hungarian Transport Firms Hit by UK Tariffs on Logistics Services

Hungary’s transportation and logistics industry is facing mounting challenges after the United Kingdom imposed new tariffs last week on logistics services and freight transport originating from Hungary. The measure, which took effect on Monday, has already resulted in notable disruptions and increased costs for Hungarian transport firms operating routes to and from the UK.

The tariffs, ranging from 10% to 15% depending on the type of service, were introduced as part of a broader review of UK trade policy. According to industry representatives, the move has had immediate effects on cross-border road freight, customs brokerage, and warehousing services provided by Hungarian companies.

Waberer's International Nyrt, one of Hungary’s leading logistics providers, confirmed on Thursday that the tariffs “significantly undermine the competitiveness of Hungarian transport operators in the UK market.” In a statement, the company noted that it is currently assessing the full financial impact and potential adjustments to its UK operations.

Péter Kovács, spokesperson for the Hungarian Association of Road Transporters, said, “We are already seeing delays at ports and rising administrative burdens. Many of our members are facing tough decisions about whether to continue serving UK clients under these conditions.”

Ferenc Horváth, an analyst at Budapest-based MarketLog Consulting, estimated that the tariffs could lead to a 20% reduction in Hungarian transport volumes to the UK over the coming months if the policy remains in place. “The additional cost is difficult to pass on to customers in an already competitive sector,” Horváth explained.

Smaller firms such as DunaSped Trans Kft. have reported cancelled contracts and a drop in new bookings. “We had to halt some of our regular weekly shipments because the margins have become unsustainable,” said Zoltán Nagy, the company’s managing director.

The Hungarian government has called for urgent talks with UK officials in hopes of resolving the dispute, but as of Friday, the tariffs remain in force, leaving the industry in a state of uncertainty.
